newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala coffee harvest slightly delayed.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala coffee harvest slightly delayed.

text.p: The coffee harvest has been slightly delayed by weather and exports will follow suit for two months, the Guatemalan coffee exporters association said Tuesday.
"In general terms the harvest is 30 to 40 days behind," Eduardo Gonzalez, president of the Coffee Exporters Association (ADEC), told Reuters.
Gonzalez said in some regions the harvest is normal, or even ahead of schedule, but in others, heavy rains held up ripening of beans for more than a month.
"We can expect for the next two months slightly low (export) volumes," said Gonzalez.

In other coffee export news, Max Quirin, president of the National Coffee Association (ANACAFE) told daily newspaper Prensa Libre the association hopes a government anti-corruption audit of ports will solve coffee theft in the ports.
The robbery of cargo containers from ports before shipment has plagued coffee exporters off and on for years, said Gonzalez.
Stricter controls in the ports could reduce the problem, he said.
According to Gonzalez coffee exporters hope the crackdown in the ports will mean a greater agility for exports and cost reductions in the long run.
